Joint Standing Committee on Transportation

Thursday, February 27, 2025

Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, and Members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation:

My name is Senator Brad Farrin; and I am before you today to testify in support of LD 289 "Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Bingham the Barry A. DeLong Bridge."

Barry's career began with the Maine State Police in 1973 when he became a Senior Detective and was known for his dedication as a child abuse investigator. In fact,
work set a record for the most child abuse convictions in New England. After
retiring from the State Police, Barry served five terms as Somerset County Sheriff, where he oversaw the construction of a new correctional facility and led the
department through significant improvements.

Beyond his professional life, Barry was a devoted family man and a trusted community leader. He gave his time to local organizations such as the Bingham Lions Club, coached youth sports, and helped organize community events. He was
always there for anyone in need, offering guidance and support whenever it was

required.

.

Barry had a love for animals, especially his beloved Jack Russell Terrier Corky. He
was always ready to lend a helping hand, whether for his family, his community, or
the people he worked with.

Naming this bridge after Barry would honor a man whose legacy of service, compassion, and leadership has had a lasting impact on everyone who knew him.

Thank you for considering this bill.

TESTIMONY IN FAVOR OF LD 289 Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Bingham the Barry A Delong Bridge
February 26, 2025
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts, honorable members of the Joint Standing Committee on Transportation. I am Jack Ducharme, and I have the honor of representing the citizens of Maine House District 71 which includes the towns of Cornville, Norridgewock, and Madison in Somerset County. I am here today to introduce my bill, LD 289, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Bingham the Barry A Delong Bridge.
Typically, such a Resolve is sponsored by the Representative of the District, in this case District 72, Liz Caruso. The widow of Sheriff Delong lives in Madison and the family had contacted me in the spring of 2024, shortly after Barry's death to put this resolution in. When Rep. Caruso was elected, I told her about the Resolve and she agreed to be a cosponsor. (This is the backstory as to why the District 71 rep is playing in District 72.)
Barry A Delong was born in Presque Isle, Maine in 1948. He was proud to be from Aroostook County and often called it "God's Country." Barry was a graduate of Presque Isle High School in 1967, where upon graduation he enrolled in Northern Maine Vocational Technical Institute for automotive, and graduated in 1970. He worked as a mechanic for two years before his career would take an unexpected twist. In 1973, Barry joined the Maine State Police, where he started as a dispatcher, progressing to later on be a Patrol Trooper, to then a Senior Detective. While working as a Senior Detective, Barry was a devoted
District 71 Cornville, Madison, and Norridgewock

child abuse investigator, and holds the record in New England for the most child abuse convictions. He had a love for children, and would have adopted them all if it had been possible. Barry retired from the Maine State Police in 1993, but knew his work was far from being finished, and due to the love of the people of Somerset County, he decided to run for Somerset Sheriff in 1994. Barry won the election and was declared High Sheriff where he served his role for 5 terms, holding the longest tenure of any Sheriff in county history. During his time as Sheriff, Barry oversaw many changes and advancements at the department, including the 2008 construction of the new $22 million correctional facility, designed to replace the old facility that had been built in 1895. Barry transformed every aspect of the department for the better, for the employees and the Somerset citizens. He was a smart businessman who always looked out for the taxpayer, kept business local to help his community. Barry retired in 2014.
While he was Sheriff, Barry was an active citizen in his community and belonged to many organizations throughout the years including President of Bingham Lions Club, Somerset Republican Party, National Police Association, National Sheriff's Association, Maine State Retired Police, Commander Sons of American Legion #99, Eagles Club, and many more. Barry taught Webelo's in Bingham, put together a softball team to get kids off the streets, helped to organize several parades (he loved parades), and volunteered at several functions for his community. Barry was the local counselor as well, not by trade but by his great advice that he would give. People trusted him because they knew he truly cared about them, even if he did not know you. He was a big believer in second chances and had full faith in people to turn their lives around, all they needed was a little help, and a bit of guidance.
In Barry's retirement, after his first wife Connie-Jo passed away, Barry met and married Suzanne Johnston of Madison. Barry and Suzanne celebrated their wedding ceremony on beautiful Mount Kineo in Greenville Maine, surrounded by the beauty of nature. Together, they enjoyed the love of the outdoors, going 4 wheeling, taking walks, and most of all gardening. Barry loved to plant and care for his gardens; he was always so proud of them. Barry and Suzanne loved going for summer rides in his Corvette, where
District 71 Cornville, Madison, and Norridgewock

there may have been a few drag racing moments here and there. Barry passed away on May 12, 2023. As a long time, personal friend of Barry, it is my honor to submit this Resolve to honor his service to the people of Somerset County and the State of Maine. Naming bridge #2027 the Barry A Delong Bridge would be a lasting tribute to this man who gave so much of his life to the residents of "God's Country on earth", that is Somerset County, Maine! I have uploaded a letter of support from the Select Board of the Town of Bingham for your consideration and review. I would appreciate your support for this Bridge naming honor for a very special man. Thank you for your time and I would be happy to answer any questions. Cordially, Jack Ducharme Jack Ducharme
District 71 Cornville, Madison, and Norridgewock

Testimony of Meghan Russo Maine Department of Transportation
Before the 132'"! Legislature, Joint Standing Committee on Transportation
Neither For Nor Against
LD 289, Resolve, to Rename a Bridge in Bingham the Barry A. Delong Bridge
Senator Nangle, Representative Crafts and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Transportation, I am Meghan Russo, Director of Government Affairs at
MaineDOT. MaineDOT is neither for nor against LD 289.
MaineDOT considers the naming of bridges, roadways, and other state transportation infrastructure to be within the purview of the Legislature. Simply put, we build them and you name them. Accordingly, we generally do not take positions on so-called "naming bills." However, we usually submit written testimony regarding whether the particular infrastructure under consideration has been named before, and if so what those name(s) are. In this case, we
are not aware of any previous legislatively-sanctioned names for the bridge identified in the
proposed amendment language. MaineDOT's current inventory number for this structure is
2027.
Thank you.
